# SB-1043 Safety bulletin: arc flash at the induction power cabinet

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P3, line P3-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L4-HT02

Hazard description
This bulletin addresses an arc flash event that occurred at the induction power cabinet feeding EQ-P3-L4-HT02. An arc flash at this cabinet can produce intense thermal energy, molten metal ejection, pressure waves and sound energy capable of causing severe burns, hearing damage and secondary trauma from unprotected workers being thrown or struck by flying objects. The induction power cabinet contains high-voltage switching components, power electronics and buswork that can accumulate stored energy even when controls indicate an off condition. In the context of heat treat operations, the cabinet energizes induction coils used to bring furnace workloads to the austenitizing setpoint for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P3-L4-HT02) of 885 °C. The high energy required to reach and maintain that setpoint increases the potential severity of any unplanned electrical discharge.

Background and incident rationale
The bulletin consolidates lessons from a near-miss event and an engineering review. Contributing factors included inadequate application of lockout/tagout for stored-energy circuits, incomplete verification of de-energized status for power electronics modules, and inconsistent use of arc-rated personal protective equipment by maintenance personnel. Human factors contributed where work planning did not clearly delineate responsibilities for isolating control power versus main power, and where documentation did not explicitly require verification steps for capacitive or inductive storage in the cabinet. The rationale for the controls below is to reduce probability of occurrence and to minimize consequence if an arc flash develops while personnel are present.

Affected equipment
- Induction power cabinet feeding EQ-P3-L4-HT02.  
- Associated control panels and disconnects that serve the induction power cabinet.  
- Work performed on or near the cabinet during maintenance, troubleshooting, testing, or installation activities on EQ-P3-L4-HT02.

Required controls
Controls apply to all personnel who plan, supervise or perform work on the affected equipment. These controls are mandatory and intended to be used in combination.

- Administrative controls
  - Work Permit: All work on the induction power cabinet requires a written work permit issued by the maintenance supervisor. The permit must reference relevant procedures in SOP-P3-L4-02 and SOP-P3-L4-05 and the maintenance record MM-P3-L4-HT02-S2.
  - Pre-job Brief: Conduct a pre-job brief that documents energy sources, responsible persons, planned isolation steps, and required PPE. Include a verification checklist that confirms removal of control and auxiliary power, and identification of components with stored energy.
  - Records: Maintain the completed permit, checklist and verification sign-off in the maintenance history for EQ-P3-L4-HT02 and file against MM-P3-L4-HT02-S2.

- Isolation and verification
  - Lockout/Tagout: Apply lockout/tagout to all energy sources feeding the induction power cabinet using the site LOTO process. De-energize control power, main power, and any local battery or capacitor blocks before accessing live parts.
  - Stored Energy: Discharge or isolate capacitors and inductive components per manufacturer recommendations before exposing terminals. Verification must be performed by a qualified electrician and documented on the permit.
  - Test for de-energized state: Use appropriately rated test instruments to verify absence of voltage. Verification is required by two people: the person performing the test and an independent verifier. Document results on the permit and retain with MM-P3-L4-HT02-S2.

- Personal protective equipment and safe approach
  - Arc-rated PPE: When exposure to potential arc flash hazards cannot be eliminated, workers must wear arc-rated PPE appropriate for the task, inspect PPE before use and follow manufacturer limitations. Use insulated tools and maintain safe distances from exposed conductors.
  - Barrier and signage: Install physical barriers and warning signage to prevent unauthorized access during work. Communicate the hazard and required PPE to all personnel in the area.

- Work controls and procedures
  - Qualified personnel only: Only qualified electrical personnel shall perform work that could expose them to arc flash hazards. Supervision must ensure competence in procedures referenced in SOP-P3-L4-02 and SOP-P3-L4-05.
  - Energized work: Energized work on the induction power cabinet is prohibited unless a formal exception is approved by the plant electrical manager and documented on the work permit, with a specific justification and mitigations.
  - Post-work verification: After reassembly and removal of LOTO, perform an insulated visual inspection and functional test before returning the cabinet to service. Document test outcomes in MM-P3-L4-HT02-S2.

Examples and scenario guidance
- Example scenario: A maintenance technician plans to replace a control module. Following this bulletin, the technician obtains a written permit, applies LOTO to control and main sources, discharges any capacitors, uses a rated voltage tester to verify absence of voltage and records the verification. PPE is used when exposed conductors are present and an independent verifier signs off prior to entry.
- Troubleshooting under power: If troubleshooting requires power to be applied for instrumentation or observation, use remote monitoring where possible, and employ isolation blocks to eliminate exposure to high-energy circuits. Any such activity must follow the energized work exception process described above.

Records to keep
- Work permits and pre-job checklists for every task on the induction power cabinet. Store copies in the maintenance file for EQ-P3-L4-HT02 and reference MM-P3-L4-HT02-S2.
- Verification tests and sign-offs performed by qualified personnel. Retain with the associated permit and note any corrective actions taken.
- Training and qualification records for personnel authorized to work on EQ-P3-L4-HT02. Cross-reference training records with SOP-P3-L4-02 and SOP-P3-L4-05 requirements.
- Incident or near-miss reports and root-cause analyses resulting from any arc events involving the cabinet.

Effective date
Effective date: Upon release

Related documents
MM-P3-L4-HT02-S2  
SOP-P3-L4-02  
SOP-P3-L4-05

Distribution and compliance
This bulletin is distributed to plant leadership, maintenance supervision, electrical staff and safety personnel at P3, line P3-L4. Compliance will be verified during scheduled maintenance audits and incident investigations. Noncompliance must be reported to the plant electrical manager for corrective action and documented in MM-P3-L4-HT02-S2.
